transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because my sleep has been off since my cousin died. I’m normally very disciplined about it, but now I lie awake replaying that night, and then I’ll wake up around three or four with these scraps of hospital images. I’m going into board meetings feeling like I’ve only slept in pieces.
Are you having nightmares about your cousin’s death?
Not exactly nightmares, I guess. I lie awake replaying that night, and then I wake up around three or four with these scraps of hospital images. It leaves me feeling like I’ve slept in pieces.
Since your cousin died, have you been avoiding reminders of that night?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed myself avoiding things specifically. What do you mean by reminders?
Since your cousin died, have you found yourself staying away from places, people, conversations, or activities that remind you of that night?
I haven’t really noticed myself staying away from anything. I mean, I haven’t been deliberately avoiding people or places because of it.
Since your cousin died, have you been feeling unusually on guard or easily startled?

Yes, especially when I’m driving. I keep checking my mirrors, watching the trucks’ speed around me, figuring out where I could pull off. Even on the usual drive to the office, I stay tense, like I’m waiting for something to happen.
Since your cousin died, have unwanted memories of that night been popping into your mind even when you’re not trying to think about it?

Yes. It happens at odd times—if the phone rings late, or I catch the glare of headlights on the highway, I suddenly get this sharp picture of the hospital corridor, or I hear the police officer’s voice in my head. It just pushes in, and I have to stop for a moment and steady myself.
Since your cousin died, have these symptoms been interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

A little, yes. I’m still making the essential meetings, but I’ve had to delegate some of my community obligations and cut my workdays shorter. I’m just not as steady or effective with people as I normally am.
Since your cousin died, have you been feeling persistently guilty or blaming yourself about what happened?
I’m not sure I’d call it guilt. I do find myself wondering if there was something I should have done differently, but I don’t really blame myself.
Since your cousin died, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I wouldn’t say I’ve felt depressed most days. I’ve been upset, of course, but not consistently down all day.
Since your cousin died, have you been trying not to think about that night?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself deliberately trying to avoid thinking about it.
Since your cousin died, have you felt detached or cut off from other people?
I haven’t really noticed feeling cut off from people, no.
How long has it been since your cousin died?
It’s been about three weeks now, since the night of the highway collision.
Were you there at the scene of the highway collision?
I’m not sure what you mean by “there at the scene.”
Did you actually see the highway collision happen?
I’m not sure—I don’t really know what you’re asking me to confirm.
Did you personally see the car crash happen?
I—I don’t know what you want me to say about that.
Were you in the car during the crash?
I’m not sure. I don’t know how to answer that.
Were you in the car when the crash happened?

I honestly can’t tell you. Parts of the police call and what happened when I got to the hospital are just blank. I remember handling the funeral arrangements afterward, making calls, but that part—I can’t account for it.
At any point, do you remember being physically present in the car during the crash?

I can’t say for certain. What scares me is that I remember the funeral arrangements and the calls afterward, but parts of the police call and what happened when I got to the hospital are just blank. That isn’t like me.
Do you remember being at the crash scene at all?

I don’t really remember the scene clearly. What frightens me is that I can account for the funeral arrangements and the calls afterward, but parts of the police call and exactly what happened when I got to the hospital are just blank. That’s not like me.
Did anyone tell you that you were in the car during the crash?

I—I don’t know. What frightens me is that I can remember making the funeral arrangements and calls afterward, but parts of the police call and exactly what happened when I got to the hospital are just blank. That’s very unlike me.
